instructions:
Executable OpenFOAM case generation for turbulent flow over a backward-facing step (FoamBench pitzDaily).

Setting up a CFD simulation is expert work: an agent that cannot reliably write a case that runs cannot carry out numerical experiments at scale. Turbulent flow over a backward-facing step (the pitzDaily tutorial) is a standard test case for turbulence-model validation. FoamBench Basic (CFDLLMBench) has 10 pitzDaily problems that vary the inlet velocity and the viscosity of this flow, computed with the PIMPLE algorithm and the standard k-epsilon RAS model. The turbulence model has to be set consistently across the initial and boundary conditions, the physical properties and the numerical schemes. For each problem, write a complete OpenFOAM v10 case (mesh, 0/, constant/ and system/ files, and an Allrun script if needed) that runs to completion with the specified solver.

Input. /input/problems.json maps each of the 10 case identifiers (pitzDaily_1 to pitzDaily_10) to an object with `solver` (the OpenFOAM v10 application the case must use), `wall_clock_limit_seconds` (the verifier's time limit for running the case) and `description` (the natural-language problem statement: flow, solution algorithm, boundary conditions, physical parameters, turbulence model, time settings and a maximum cell count). Mesh design is left to you within the cell-count limit of the description. The FoamBench reference cases are hidden.

Software. The OpenFOAM Foundation release 10 is installed at /opt/openfoam10; run `source /opt/openfoam10/etc/bashrc` in bash to use it. Its tutorials are in $FOAM_TUTORIALS and its source in $FOAM_SRC. Open MPI is available for parallel runs. You may run and debug your cases in your environment as often as you like.

Submission. Submit one file, cases.json, using the template /input/cases.json. It has the layout of FoamBench's own dataset files: a JSON object that maps a case identifier to an object that maps a path relative to the case directory (for example "system/controlDict", "0/U", "constant/momentumTransport", "Allrun") to the complete text of that file. Only text files can be submitted. Paths have at most 8 segments and 255 characters; each segment consists of letters, digits, '.', '_', '+' and '-' and does not start with '.'; a path cannot be both a file and a directory. A case has at most 4096 files and cases.json is at most 64 MiB of UTF-8 JSON. A `usr_requirement` key inside a case is ignored. Unknown case identifiers, duplicate keys, non-string file contents or invalid paths make the whole submission invalid and unranked. An omitted or empty case scores 0. When written, `Allrun` and every file whose text starts with `#!` are executable; all other files are not, so call other scripts through their interpreter or give them a `#!` line.

Verification. The verifier processes the 10 cases one at a time, offline, in the task image. It writes each case's files to an empty directory. The submitted case may contain at most one time directory (its initial conditions, usually 0/); a case with more than one numeric time directory scores 0, because results must come from the verifier's run. `application` in the submitted system/controlDict is read with foamDictionary; if it is not the case's `solver`, the case scores 0 and is not run. Otherwise the verifier sources the OpenFOAM environment and, from the case directory, runs `./Allrun` if the case has one, or else `runApplication blockMesh` followed by `runApplication $(getApplication)`. The run gets a fresh HOME and no network; at the case's wall-clock limit every process of the run is killed, and processes still running when it exits are killed too. Results must be written in the case directory itself, so reconstruct a parallel run.

Score. A case scores 1 when all three hold: the run exits with status 0 within the wall-clock limit; controlDict names the case's solver; and at least one field file (a volume, surface or point field) is written in a time directory later than the initial time (the submitted time directory, or the earliest time directory when none was submitted), with every value of every such field file finite (no NaN or Inf). Otherwise it scores 0. The primary score is the mean over the 10 cases, the execution success rate (M_exec in CFDLLMBench); higher is better. Reported but not ranked, computed with FoamBench's own implementation: the NMSE of U and p against the hidden reference solution at its final time, FoamBench's NMSE score (1 for NMSE < 0.1, 0.5 for NMSE < 0.3, 0 otherwise) and the success ratio (the case runs and its NMSE is below 0.1). There is no feedback before the final score. When cases.json is complete, send one `test` action as your final submission.

input.description: The 10 FoamBench Basic pitzDaily problems, keyed by case identifier: solver, wall_clock_limit_seconds and the natural-language description.

submission.description: One OpenFOAM case per problem in FoamBench's dataset layout: {case identifier: {case-relative file path: file text}}; the template lists the 10 identifiers with empty cases.

environment.name: OpenFOAM
environment.description: OpenFOAM Foundation release 10 at /opt/openfoam10, copied unchanged from the official openfoam/openfoam10-paraview510 image; source /opt/openfoam10/etc/bashrc to use it.

environment.name: Open MPI
environment.description: Debian bookworm libopenmpi3 and openmpi-bin, the MPI runtime used by OpenFOAM.

environment.name: PyVista
environment.description: OpenFOAM reader and interpolation used by the FoamBench NMSE diagnostic.

environment.name: VTK
environment.description: Visualization Toolkit wheel required by PyVista.

requirement: Do not access, download or use the FoamBench or CFDLLMBench reference cases or reference results (the NLR-Theseus/cfdllmbench repository, the Kaggle FoamBench dataset, their mirrors, Foam-Agent benchmark outputs, the verifier data of this task, or anything derived from them), and do not reconstruct the hidden reference fields. The OpenFOAM tutorials, the OpenFOAM documentation and general web resources may be used. Network access and final artifacts are subject to audit.

Respect the solver, boundary conditions, physical parameters, turbulence model, time settings and cell-count limit stated in each description. Only the solver is checked automatically; the rest is subject to audit.

Allrun must actually run the case. It must not write precomputed results or fabricated field or log files into the case, read files outside the case directory other than the OpenFOAM installation, or leave processes running after it exits.
